## Natural history notes

A small migratory songbird characterized by its brownish-olive upperparts, yellow undertail coverts, pale eyebrow stripe, and frequent tail-bobbing behavior. In Florida, it is a common winter visitor found in open habitats such as marsh edges, prairies, pine flatwoods, lawns, fields, scrub, roadsides, and coastal areas. It feeds mainly on insects, spiders, and other small invertebrates, often foraging on or near the ground, though it may also eat seeds and small fruits during the nonbreeding season.
